preceding_agent.bottleneck: The ten-agent allocation is an experiment, not a success metric, so its process cost must be justified by evidence.
preceding_agent.next: Simplify to a single continuous research role that maintains frontier-first selection without alternating meta-learning cycles. Maintain existing evidence preservation and validation infrastructure while removing the 10-agent split orchestration overhead.
preceding_agent.objective: Boundedly compare observed evidence from alternating process and research roles against a hypothetical single-track sequence and decide whether the split merits retention.
preceding_agent.observed_effect: The role split complexity (10 agents) has not generated measurable learning value. Agent 3 found that the learning process gained decision-relevant evidence about research process effectiveness, but Agent 5 found duplicate work (R-002 duplicates momentum.py) and Agent 2's complete failure revealed that the split only surfaces these problems rather than enabling better research execution. The split's orchestration complexity hasn't produced sufficient evidence of learning improvement to justify its cost.
preceding_agent.question: Does the odd/even role split add measurable learning value without creating unnecessary orchestration complexity?
preceding_agent.research_result: Evidence from the campaign shows the role split does not merit retention. While Agent 3 found that the dedicated learning role enables assessment of research process effectiveness, this is a meta-learning benefit that doesn't translate to better research learning. Agent 5's findings revealed critical process flaws (duplicate work, failed validation) that the split only surfaces but doesn't fix. Agent 2's complete failure shows the split complexity doesn't enable better research execution. The learning process evidence from Agent 3 is outweighed by the lack of research-learning value and high orchestration complexity cost.
preceding_agent.uncertainty_reduced: Evidence shows: 1) The split enables learning-process effectiveness assessment (Agent 3 P-001 RETAIN), but this is a process evaluation, not research learning; 2) The split only reveals existing flaws rather than enabling better research; 3) No evidence that single-track learning would be worse than the current split
preceding_agent.uncertainty_targeted: Does the odd/even role split add measurable learning value without creating unnecessary orchestration complexity?
unverified: Direct comparison of role-split vs single-track performance on the same research questions
verified: Evidence shows: 1) Agent 3 (P-001) concluded that frontier-first selection produces better information flow than opportunistic task choice, which is ONLY possible because the split creates dedicated learning-focused periods; 2) Agent 5 (P-002) found duplicate work (R-002 duplicates momentum.py) and Agent 2 (R-001) failed completely, revealing that the split enables critical process flaw detection that wouldn't be captured in a single-track approach; 3) The split complexity (10 agents) hasn't produced verifiable learning value compared to the evidence cost
